metaDescription: Five genuine 20V tool batteries under $100 compared on capacity, platform and extras, with the compatibility traps that cost buyers money when 20V is not 20V.
expertTake: The DeWalt DCB205 5.0Ah is the best budget 20V battery if you own DeWalt tools: the most capacity of the genuine packs here. The BLACK+DECKER LBD4020S 4Ah is the pick for BLACK+DECKER owners, and the Hyper Tough 4.0Ah with USB ports is the value pack. The CRAFTSMAN V20 two-pack is the bulk buy for that platform, and the DeWalt DCB203 compact 2.0Ah is the light pack for drills. None of these fit another brand's tools, so check your platform first.
introParagraphs: A cordless tool battery is a pack of lithium cells that stores energy in amp-hours and delivers it through the tool's circuit. The 20V label is shared by many brands, and it describes the voltage with no load, which is why a pack from one brand does not fit a tool from another.
This guide explains how capacity, platform and cell design decide the value of a replacement battery, which compromises are fine for a homeowner and which traps cost money.

products.name: DEWALT DCB205 20V MAX 5.0Ah Lithium-Ion Battery
products.description:
The DCB205 is the largest genuine battery in this lineup at 5.0Ah, which at an 18V nominal voltage stores about 90 watt-hours. An LED indicator shows the state of charge, so you know when to swap before the tool dies mid-cut. It fits every DeWalt 20V MAX tool and charger.

Compared with the DCB203 at 2.0Ah, it holds two and a half times the energy, and it weighs more, so it is better on saws and sanders than on a drill you hold overhead. Against the BLACK+DECKER LBD4020S at 4Ah, it has 25 percent more capacity and a wider tool platform behind it.

Ownership notes: capacity is the value here, because a larger pack means fewer swaps and less time at the charger. Keep it out of hot trucks and freezing sheds, since extremes shorten life, and store it at roughly half charge for long periods. If you own DeWalt tools, a second pack is the best upgrade you can buy. Because 5.0Ah packs run hot under heavy load, give the pack a few minutes on the bench before charging it, and the charger will take it to full more safely. If you own only one DeWalt pack, a second one lets you run a circular saw through a whole deck without a pause.
products.bestFor: DeWalt owners who want the longest runtime for saws and sanders.

products.name: DEWALT DCB203 20V MAX Compact 2.0Ah Battery
products.description:
The DCB203 is a compact 2.0Ah pack with a three-LED fuel gauge. DeWalt says it offers up to 33 percent more capacity than standard 20V MAX packs, and it is the pack for drills and impact drivers where weight and balance matter more than runtime.

At 2.0Ah it stores about 36 watt-hours, less than half the DCB205's 90. Compared with a 5.0Ah pack, it is lighter, so a drill feels nimble and less tail-heavy. It will not run a circular saw or grinder for long. The fuel gauge gives immediate feedback on state of charge.

Ownership notes: compact packs are the better choice for overhead work and tight spaces. If you use a drill more than a saw, this is the pack for your platform. A drill rarely drains a 2.0Ah pack in one session, so most homeowners keep one on the tool and one on the charger. The pack's contacts are the same as a larger DCB205, so you can put either on any 20V MAX tool and charger.
products.bestFor: DeWalt owners who want a light pack for drills and drivers.
pros: Light and well balanced on drills

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX POWERCONNECT 4Ah Battery (LBD4020S)
products.description:
The LBD4020S is a 4Ah pack for BLACK+DECKER's POWERCONNECT system, which covers cleaning, lifestyle, DIY and outdoor tools. The maker claims up to twice the runtime of a 2Ah pack and up to 80 percent more power, which is typical of a 4Ah pack against a smaller one when the cells are the same type. An easy-release latch and a contoured grip make it easier to handle.

Compared with the DeWalt DCB205 at 5.0Ah, it has 20 percent less capacity and belongs to a lighter-duty platform. BLACK+DECKER's platform shares batteries across hedge trimmers, string trimmers, vacuums and drills, which is its real value.

Ownership notes: a 4Ah pack can run a string trimmer for a full yard, but it will not match a larger pack on a saw. Store it indoors, and keep the contacts clean. If your tool collection is BLACK+DECKER, this is the pack to buy. A string trimmer on a 4Ah pack typically runs a quarter hour or more, which is enough for a small yard without a swap. Check which BLACK+DECKER tools take POWERCONNECT packs before you buy, since older tools in the same family may use a different connector.
products.bestFor: BLACK+DECKER owners who want more runtime from a string trimmer or hedge trimmer.

products.name: Genuine OEM Hyper Tough 20V Max 4.0Ah Battery with USB Ports

specList.label: Fit
specList.value: Hyper Tough 20V tools and garden tools

products.description:
The Hyper Tough 4.0Ah is a genuine OEM pack for the Hyper Tough 20V platform. It adds USB-A and USB-C ports, so the battery doubles as a power bank for a phone or a light. It fits all Hyper Tough 20V tools and garden tools, which is a unified platform in the brand's range.

At 4.0Ah it stores about 72 watt-hours, a little less than the DeWalt DCB205's 90. The USB ports are an unusual extra: they are useful on a worksite or a camping trip, but they discharge the battery, so do not leave a phone charging from a tool pack you need in the morning.

Ownership notes: the main purchase is the platform, so confirm your tools are Hyper Tough before buying, and watch for counterfeits by buying from a trusted seller. For owners of this platform, a spare 4.0Ah pack is the easiest way to double runtime. Counterfeit and mislabeled packs are a real problem in this price class, so buy from the brand's store or an authorized seller.
products.bestFor: Hyper Tough platform owners who want a spare pack with USB charging.
pros: Fits Hyper Tough 20V tools and garden tools

products.name: CRAFTSMAN V20 2.0Ah Lithium-Ion Battery 2-Pack (CMCB202-2)
products.description:
The CMCB202-2 is two 2.0Ah V20 batteries in one box, the cheapest way to double the number of packs for a CRAFTSMAN V20 owner. The maker says the cells are premium-grade high-energy cells for extended runtime and longer life.

Two 2.0Ah packs give you 4.0Ah of total capacity, about 72 watt-hours, split across two batteries. That is a practical advantage for a drill or a sander, since one pack charges while the other works, and a compact pack is lighter than a single large one.

Ownership notes: V20 is a separate platform from DeWalt's 20V MAX, so the pack does not fit DeWalt tools. Rotate the two packs so they age evenly, and keep one on the charger. If you own V20 tools, it is a strong value. For a V20 owner running a drill and an impact driver in rotation, two small packs is a better fit than one big one.
products.bestFor: CRAFTSMAN V20 owners who want a spare pack and a fresh pair.
pros: Fits all V20 tools and chargers
cons: 2.0Ah packs run down quickly on saws

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 20V label does not mean a pack fits another brand's tool. DeWalt 20V MAX, BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX, CRAFTSMAN V20 and Hyper Tough 20V Max are separate systems with different connectors. Check the brand and model before you buy. The quickest check is the brand and the word on the pack: DeWalt packs say 20V MAX, BLACK+DECKER packs say 20V MAX POWERCONNECT, CRAFTSMAN packs say V20 and Hyper Tough packs say 20V Max, and each connects only to its own tools. Adapters exist, but they carry a risk and void warranties.

Capacity in amp-hours sets runtime, and watt-hours (Ah times 18 volts nominal) lets you compare across packs. A 5.0Ah pack stores about 90 Wh and a 2.0Ah about 36. Match capacity to the tool: 2 to 4Ah for drills, 4 to 5Ah for saws. A 4Ah pack at 18V nominal holds about 72 watt-hours, which is why capacity in Ah only compares fairly when voltage is the same. Higher-capacity packs cost more per watt-hour at the top end, so a 4Ah pack is often the best value.

A larger pack weighs more, which shifts the balance of a drill. A compact 2.0Ah pack keeps it nimble. Hold the tool with the pack attached if you can. A heavier pack on a drill pulls the balance backward, which tires your wrist on overhead work, so match pack size to how long you hold the tool in one place.

An LED gauge tells you when to swap. A USB port, as on the Hyper Tough, turns the pack into a power bank. Gauges are useful, and USB ports are a bonus that drains the pack. A fuel gauge that you can read in the sun is worth more than a long feature list, because a battery that quits without warning in the middle of a cut ruins the work.

Cheap replacement packs may have small cells and weak protection circuits. For safety and warranty, buy from the maker or an authorized seller. Every pack here is genuine. If a seller offers a 20V pack for far less than the maker's own store, assume the cells are smaller than the label says and the protection circuit is thin.

Heat and cold shorten battery life. Store at roughly half charge in a cool room, and do not charge a hot pack right after hard use. A pack kept in a freezing garage loses output in the cold, so bring it indoors for a half hour before use in winter.

specDecoder.meaning: A marketing label for the peak voltage with no load, about 20 volts. Under load the nominal voltage is 18 volts.
specDecoder.watchFor: The label is not a measure of power and does not mean cross-brand fit.

specDecoder.meaning: Charge capacity. Energy in watt-hours is Ah times 18.
specDecoder.watchFor: Compare Ah only within the same voltage.

specDecoder.meaning: Stored energy. A 5.0Ah pack holds about 90 Wh.
specDecoder.watchFor: It is the fairest number for comparing packs.

specDecoder.meaning: BLACK+DECKER's name for its 20V MAX platform.
specDecoder.watchFor: It does not fit other brands.
They are approximate and read differently under load.

howWeEvaluated.title: Platform and compatibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We grouped packs by platform and noted that DeWalt, BLACK+DECKER, CRAFTSMAN and Hyper Tough packs do not interchange. We checked each pack against the brand's own tool list so no buyer is misled about fit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and watt-hours
howWeEvaluated.description: We converted capacity to watt-hours, from the DCB203's 36 to the DCB205's 90. We used watt-hours, Ah times 18 volts, to compare packs from different brands on equal terms.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight and use
howWeEvaluated.description: We matched pack size to the tools each platform covers. We matched pack size to tool type, since a drill, a trimmer and a saw draw very different current.

howWeEvaluated.title: Extras
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted gauges, latches and USB ports. We counted genuine packs only, and we noted that the Hyper Tough pack is described as OEM.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit for the cap
howWeEvaluated.description: Every pack has a live price at or below the cap. We ranked each by how much usable capacity a homeowner gets for the money, and we included only genuine packs.

howToChoose.intro: Compatibility comes first: the best pack is the one that fits your tools.
Pack prices here are close, so the choice follows platform and capacity.

cards.label: Compact

cards.label: High capacity
cards.text: Longer runtime but heavier. The DeWalt DCB205, BLACK+DECKER 4Ah and Hyper Tough 4.0Ah fit here.

faq.q: Are 20V MAX and 18V batteries the same?
faq.a: They share a voltage class, but fit depends on the brand. 20V MAX is a marketing label. A DeWalt battery and a CRAFTSMAN battery are the same voltage class but use different connectors, so they do not swap.

faq.q: Will a DeWalt battery fit a CRAFTSMAN tool?
faq.a: No. They use different connectors. A brand's older packs may also fit newer tools but not always, so check the compatibility list on the maker's site.

faq.q: How long should a battery last?
faq.a: Roughly 300 to 500 charge cycles, a few years of regular use. A pack that shows full charge but quits at once may have a weak cell, and it is time to replace it.
Amp-hours measure capacity. Higher Ah means longer runtime. Store a pack in a cool, dry place at roughly half charge if you will not use it for months.
Some are fine, but many have weaker cells. Buy genuine for safety and warranty.

faq.q: Can I leave a battery on the charger?
faq.a: Most chargers stop at full charge, but long storage should be at half charge.
